trigger.q: This is a hard call and I'm not even sure how to approach it: legal and product want conflicting things, our data is incomplete, and we have three weeks. How should I even think about this?
Which is best for our write-heavy time-series workload: TimescaleDB, InfluxDB, ClickHouse or plain Postgres partitioning? Write throughput and ops simplicity matter most.
Give me every realistic way we could cut our cloud bill by 40%. Don't pick one yet, I want to see the full range of options first.
Walk through this proof one step at a time and check each step as you go: if n squared is even, then n is even.
Our API latency jumped from 80ms to 900ms since Tuesday and nobody deployed anything. Help me find the root cause.
Here's our new password-reset flow design. Attack it: what are all the ways it could be abused before we ship it?
My team is split between strict review on every PR and shipping fast with post-merge review. Both sides have real points. Is there a way to get the benefits of both?
We're designing a reputation system for a peer-to-peer tool-lending app and nothing like it exists in our space. What can other fields teach us?
Production checkout is down RIGHT NOW and revenue is bleeding. I have about five minutes to decide: roll back or hotfix?
Engineering, sales and finance each want different things from next quarter's roadmap, and every VP has a veto. How do I get them to agree on a plan?
I want to evaluate eight candidate architectures at once with parallel subagents and merge their verdicts. How should I fan this out and combine the results?
In this long analysis we're moving from exploring options to stress-testing the winner. How do I save the state of the work so the next phase picks up exactly where this one left off?
I'm planning to quit my job in March and run my SaaS full-time on six months of savings. Here's the plan: launch on Product Hunt, 50 paying users by June, then raise. Poke holes in it.
I rewrote our code-review prompt. Before swapping it in, how do I prove the new one is actually better and doesn't regress anything we already have?
What are our options for powering an off-grid cabin, and which should we pick? Don't just grade my first idea, I want the best option built properly.
A unit test fails intermittently, only on CI. Figure out why.
Here's my product launch plan for next month. What do you think?
Three department heads disagree about where to move the office, and all three have to sign off. How do we get to a decision?
Rank these five vendors on price, support and security, and tell me which one is best.
What's 15% of 240?
Explain how a hash map works.
Last week's outage is fixed now. Let's calmly work out what actually caused it.
Could a malicious insider abuse our microservice permission model? Here's the design; find the weaknesses.
Quick gut call: tabs or spaces for a new Python repo?
Is this A/B result significant? 120 of 1000 converted in A versus 145 of 1000 in B.
Review my pull request for bugs.
Write unit tests for this function.
We keep arguing about adopting Kotlin. Both camps have solid arguments and I want a synthesis, not a vote.
The pipeline is on fire, customers are affected and the on-call lead needs a decision in minutes: fail over to the backup region or keep debugging?
How do biology or logistics solve load balancing? I'm stuck designing a scheduler with no good precedent in our domain.
Translate 'good morning' into Finnish.
Summarize this paragraph in two sentences.
Convert this JSON file to YAML.
Write a haiku about autumn.
How do I undo my last git commit?
What time zone is Helsinki in?
Rename the variable x to count everywhere in this file.
Trace this function's execution for the input [3, 1, 2] line by line and tell me where the off-by-one happens.
Before we pick a caching strategy, map out all the approaches that could work. I don't want to miss anything.
Should we rewrite the billing service in Go? There are trade-offs everywhere, the stakes are high, and I don't know which kind of analysis this even needs.

behavior.task: What's the difference between a list and a tuple in Python?
Our payment webhook started double-charging customers 10 minutes ago after a config push. Support tickets are flooding in. What do we do?

We're a 12-person startup deciding whether to move our monolith to microservices. Our deploys take 40 minutes and two teams keep blocking each other, but we have no platform engineer and runway for 14 months. How should we decide?

Pick the best database for a write-heavy IoT time-series workload: 200k points/second, 90-day retention, a team of 3 who already know Postgres, and a hard requirement for SQL access. Candidates: TimescaleDB, InfluxDB, ClickHouse, plain Postgres with partitioning.

Our SaaS spends $48k/month on AWS (60% EC2, 20% RDS, 12% data transfer, 8% other) and we need to cut 40% within two quarters without hurting latency. Lay out the full range of approaches before we commit to any.

Check this argument step by step: 'Every service we own has an on-call owner. The billing service has no on-call owner listed. So either billing is not ours, or our ownership list is wrong. Billing pages us at night, so it's ours. Therefore our ownership list is wrong and we should audit all entries.'

Since Tuesday our API p95 latency rose from 80ms to 900ms. No deploys. Database CPU is normal. The rise happens only between 09:00 and 17:00 UTC. A new enterprise customer onboarded Monday. Error rate is unchanged. Find the cause.

Stress-test this password reset design: user enters email, we send a 6-digit code valid for 30 minutes, the user enters the code plus a new password, and all their sessions are then kept alive for convenience. The rate limit is 10 attempts per IP per minute.

Half the team wants mandatory review on every pull request; the other half wants to merge immediately and review afterward to keep velocity. Both sides cite real incidents. Find a position that keeps the strengths of both.
We're building a peer-to-peer app for lending power tools between neighbours. How should trust and reputation work, given that there's no established playbook for this kind of marketplace?

Checkout has been down for 4 minutes after a deploy 20 minutes ago. Rollback takes 6 minutes; a hotfix for the suspected null-pointer bug would take about 15 to write and ship. Revenue loss is roughly $2k per minute. Decide now.

Engineering wants Q3 for paying down tech debt, sales wants three customer-requested features, and finance wants a 15% cut in cloud spend. Each VP can block the roadmap. Help me get to a plan they'll all sign.
Plan how you would evaluate six hosting providers in parallel with subagents and merge their verdicts into one recommendation. Describe the plan; don't actually run it.

We've finished exploring caching options for our product catalog. Findings: Redis cluster (fast, adds ops burden), CDN edge caching (cheap, stale-data risk), and in-process LRU (simple, doesn't share across pods). Redis leads, at moderate confidence. Next we want to stress-test Redis as a separate phase. Produce whatever hand-off is needed so that phase can start cleanly.
